newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to start mining tender round in February.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to start mining tender round in February.

text.p: Ecuador will call international tenders starting in February for several mining prospects, a state official said Tuesday.

"The state has some mining sites where it has not been able to continue with extensive exploration," Zoilo Angulo, head of the state's Geological and Mining Development and Investigation Corporation (Codigem), told Reuters.
He said in an interview that the state will consider the amount of money offered, investment plans, and the environmental impact of any offers made.

Ecuador's government hopes new private investment will help boost the country's gold output, which it projects will total 810,000 ounces in 1998 and 675,000 ounces this year. The country's gold output totaled 569,000 ounces last year, up from 499,000 ounces in 1995.

The Portavelo gold area will be the first to be tendered at the beginning of February. Angulo said the areas of Chahuan, Cerro Verde, Malacatos, Toisan, Las Guardias, Telimbela, Balzapampa, and Nambija 3 will follow.
The latter group of areas -- to be tendered by April at the latest -- contain gold, silver, zinc, copper, coal and platinum.
Companies which have shown early interest in bidding include Placer Dome Inc and Cambior Inc from Canada, Newmont Mining and Cyprus Amax Minerals Co, and Chile's state-owned Codelco, Angulo said.
Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, is interested in the Toisan copper prospect, the official said.
